Metadata.title: Perch Trail
Metadata.description: Perch Trail: hand-painted birdhouses on the streets of Maple Hollow. Find them on the map, walk the trail, and read the story behind each one.

HomePage.heroSubtitle: A birdhouse inspired community art experience
HomePage.heroDescription: Perch Trail is a community project to turn our neighbourhood into an open-air walking gallery of hand-painted birdhouses. Creating new experiences and colours for all to enjoy.

EventsPage.title: Events
EventsPage.subtitle: Painting sessions and neighbourhood gatherings. All are welcome.
EventsPage.comingSoonDescription: We're lining up the next painting session in Maple Hollow. Check back soon, or get in touch to hear about it first.
EventsPage.wantToHostDescription: We're always looking for spaces and organisers. Get in touch and let's make something happen.
EventsPage.kickoffWhere: Hollow Oven Bakery, 12 Orchard Row, Maple Hollow
EventsPage.kickoffDescription: We're kicking off the trail! You are invited to come help us start it with colour. Paint a birdhouse, grab a bite, and meet the neighbours behind the project. Hollow Oven Bakery is opening its doors for an afternoon of paint, good food, and good company. Birdhouses and brushes are on us; food and drinks are available to buy. Drop in any time between 1pm and 5pm. Bring a friend, bring the family, or just bring yourself and you will be welcomed into the mix. See you soon!
EventsPage.wsWhere: Kiln Lane Books, 4 Kiln Lane, Maple Hollow
EventsPage.wsDescription: Come paint a free birdhouse! Everyone's welcome: first-timers and old hands alike. There'll be music, colour, and fun for the whole family. We bring the birdhouses, paint, and brushes; you bring your imagination. Drop in any time between 2 and 6 and leave with something you made.
EventsPage.ssTitle: Winter Paint-In at the Ferry Steps
EventsPage.ssWhere: The landing at the foot of Ferry Steps, Maple Hollow
EventsPage.ssDescription: It's official: we're painting birdhouses at the Ferry Steps, the wide stone landing where the steps meet the river path at the edge of Maple Hollow. Drop in any time between 1pm and 4pm. We bring the birdhouses, paint, brushes and something warm to drink; you just bring yourself. First-timers, old hands, whole households: everyone's invited. Pull up a crate and help us bring colour to the quiet end of the neighbourhood.

VolunteerPage.title: Volunteer
VolunteerPage.subtitle: No experience required. No commitment too small. Every hand makes the trail a little better.
VolunteerPage.intro: Perch Trail is built entirely by volunteers. There are lots of ways to help, from an afternoon of postering to a season of painting events. You don't need to be an expert. You just need to show up.
VolunteerPage.lightWork: Lots of hands make light work.
VolunteerPage.posteringDescription: Help spread the word the old-fashioned way: putting up posters around the neighbourhood, on community boards, and anywhere people gather.
VolunteerPage.graphicDesignDescription: We need posters, social assets, and print materials. If you have an eye for design, your work will be seen all over Maple Hollow.
VolunteerPage.paintingHelperDescription: Help run community painting sessions: set up supplies, welcome newcomers, and make sure everyone leaves with a birdhouse they're proud of.
VolunteerPage.communityAwarenessDescription: Go door to door, talk to neighbours, and engage local businesses. Find would-be painters, hosts, and anyone who wants to be part of something good.
VolunteerPage.installerDescription: Once a birdhouse is painted, it needs a home. Help mount and install birdhouses at host locations around the neighbourhood.
VolunteerPage.moderatorDescription: Answer questions from the community, review birdhouse submissions, and help keep the project running smoothly online.
VolunteerPage.socialMediaDescription: Capture moments (painting sessions, newly installed birdhouses, neighbourhood reactions) and share them with the world.
VolunteerPage.writerDescription: Help bring the project's voice together. Write copy, tell stories, and make sure the messaging is as warm and clear as the project itself.
VolunteerPage.developerDescription: The site is kept running by one or two people in their spare time; it would be great to have someone tackle tickets and make pull requests. We'll coach you if you want to learn. The stack is Next.js, TypeScript, and Supabase.
VolunteerPage.getBirdhouseTitle: Want to get your hands on a birdhouse?
VolunteerPage.getBirdhouseDescription: Birdhouses are free. We'll set you up with everything you need: the house, paint, and a page on the trail map.
VolunteerPage.readyToHelpDescription: Drop us a note and we'll find something meaningful for you to do.

GetInvolvedPage.title: Get Involved
GetInvolvedPage.subtitle: Whether you want to paint, hang, or host a bird house, there's a place for you here.
GetInvolvedPage.paintBirdhouse: I want to paint a birdhouse
GetInvolvedPage.paintDescription: Get a free birdhouse, make it yours, then put it on the map.
GetInvolvedPage.hangBirdhouse: I want to hang a birdhouse
GetInvolvedPage.hangDescription: Have a fence, balcony, or storefront? Give a birdhouse a home and join the trail.
GetInvolvedPage.itsFreeDescription1: We give away birdhouses at no cost and if you are interested we can set up a 'perch page' for it on the trail map.
GetInvolvedPage.itsFreeDescription2: Paint it at home on your own schedule. There's no deadline, no pressure, and no wrong way to do it.
GetInvolvedPage.eventsPickupDescription: Prefer to paint with others? We run community painting sessions where you can show up, get set up, and leave with a finished birdhouse. Pickup times for take-home bird houses are posted regularly too.
GetInvolvedPage.ownIdeaDescription: Want to build your own birdhouse from scratch or do something a little different? We love that. Send us a request and we'll email you a link and access code to set up your page. Your creation joins the trail just like any other.
GetInvolvedPage.requestKitDescription: Let us know you would like a birdhouse and we'll email you back with everything you need to join the trail.
GetInvolvedPage.anySpaceDescription1: You don't need a front yard. A fence, a balcony, a storefront window, a community garden post: if it's visible from the street and you're willing to keep an eye on it, it counts. Even one birdhouse makes a difference.
GetInvolvedPage.anySpaceDescription2: Have room for more than one? Even better. We'll work with you to find the right fit.
GetInvolvedPage.privateHostingTitle: Want a birdhouse but not at your house?
GetInvolvedPage.privateHostingDescription: Some folks would rather not have a birdhouse displayed where they live. Totally fair. Just say so when you request one and we'll find a public spot to hang it on your behalf. The trail map shows the birdhouse, not the person.
GetInvolvedPage.dontHaveToBeArtist: You don't have to be the artist
GetInvolvedPage.dontHaveToBeArtistDescription1: Hosting and painting are two different things. As a host, your job is simply to provide a good spot for someone else's work to live. You're giving a local artist's birdhouse a home, and giving everyone who walks by a reason to stop.
GetInvolvedPage.dontHaveToBeArtistDescription2: Your location goes on the map. Visitors can read about the artist and the story behind the birdhouse on its page.
GetInvolvedPage.hostFormTitle: I Want to Host a Birdhouse
GetInvolvedPage.wantToHelpDescription: There's always something that needs doing: postering, painting, installing, designing, coding, or just showing up. Whatever you're good at, we can probably use it. Reach out and we'll figure it out together.

FAQPage.title: Frequently Asked Questions
FAQPage.subtitle: Everything you need to know about Perch Trail, from finding birdhouses to becoming part of the trail.
FAQPage.noResults: No questions match your search. Try a different term, or reach out to us directly.
FAQPage.faq1Answer: Perch Trail is a local, community-focused art project of hand-painted birdhouses. Each birdhouse is made by a neighbour (young and old), cared for by neighbours, and has its own (optional) page on the trail map. It's a neighbourhood project, a platform to bring people together and create a little more whimsy in our lives.
FAQPage.faq2Answer: The main trail runs along Orchard Row, between Kiln Lane and the Ferry Steps in Maple Hollow. But anyone, from anywhere, is invited to take part by hanging a birdhouse and adding it to the map in their neighbourhood. You can find every location on our [interactive map](/map); the ones along the main trail are all within walking distance of each other.
FAQPage.faq3Question: How do I get a free birdhouse to paint?
FAQPage.faq3Answer: We give away birdhouses at no cost. Pick one up at one of our painting events or request one through our [Get Involved page](/get-involved), and paint it at home on your own schedule: no deadline, no pressure. Once it's ready, send us a request and we'll email you a link and access code so you can set up its page on the trail.
FAQPage.faq4Question: Can I be an artist on the trail?
FAQPage.faq4Answer: Absolutely. You don't need a portfolio or any formal training; if you can hold a brush, you're qualified. Grab a free birdhouse, paint it however you like, send us a request, and we'll email you a link and access code to set up its page. You can name it, tell its story, add photos: all yours. Or just hang it and let it be a hidden gem to be discovered organically. Want to build your own birdhouse from scratch? That works the same way.
FAQPage.faq5Question: How do I host a birdhouse?
FAQPage.faq5Answer: If you have a fence, balcony, storefront, or any spot visible from the street, you can host. You don't have to paint it yourself either; hosting and painting are two different roles. The birdhouse's location goes on the map (if desired), and visitors can read about the artist and birdhouse on its page. Get in touch through our [Get Involved page](/get-involved) to sign up.
FAQPage.faq6Answer: No committee. No board. Perch Trail is an idea started by a handful of Maple Hollow neighbours who paint a bit, build things, and have lived on these streets a long time. There's no organisation behind it, just people who wanted to create a little more whimsy through birdhouses in their neighbourhood. The project is a platform for community building, and it wouldn't exist without the support and participation of friends, family, local neighbours, and businesses.
FAQPage.faq7Question: How do I find out about a birdhouse I see on the street?
FAQPage.faq7Answer: Many birdhouses have their own page on our website. Open the [trail map](/map), find the birdhouse near where you spotted it, and you'll see who painted it, what inspired it, and possibly who's caring for it. It's how we connect the physical art to the story behind it.
FAQPage.faq8Question: Can I donate or sponsor the project?
FAQPage.faq8Answer: Yes, please. Birdhouses are free because of community support, and every dollar goes toward materials, paint kits, events, and keeping the trail growing. If you'd like to contribute, anything and everything helps; use the contact form on the homepage to inquire. It's not expected, though; we're doing everything we can to keep this completely free for neighbours.
FAQPage.faq9Question: What happens if a birdhouse is damaged or goes missing?
FAQPage.faq9Answer: Weather, wear, and the occasional mishap are part of outdoor art. If you notice a damaged or missing birdhouse, let us know through the contact form. We'll work with the host and artist to repair or replace it. The trail is meant to be lived-in and experienced, not precious things to fawn over from afar.
FAQPage.faq10Question: What happens to the birdhouses at the end of the season?
FAQPage.faq10Answer: That depends on the host and the artist. Some birdhouses stay up year-round, some come inside for the winter, and some may be part of a future end-of-season showcase in the neighbourhood. The trail is designed to evolve; nothing is permanent, and that's part of what makes it interesting. If you're hosting birdhouses and want them removed, we'll absolutely help with that.
FAQPage.stillHaveQuestionsDescription: We'd love to hear from you. Drop us a note and we'll get back to you.
FAQPage.faq11Question: Can I chip in a few dollars?
FAQPage.faq11Answer: Yes, and thank you! Head to the [Support the Trail](/support) page, pick an amount, and we'll email you a transfer request for it. Every dollar goes straight back into paint, brushes, and birdhouses.

SupportPage.title: Keep the trail growing
SupportPage.subtitle: Perch Trail runs on paint, plywood, and neighbours like you.
SupportPage.impact: There are a few different ways to give below, whatever feels right. Perch Trail isn't a moneymaker: every dollar goes straight back into paint, plywood, and new birdhouses. Offsetting the cost just means the trail can grow faster and reach more streets.
SupportPage.honesty: Perch Trail is a neighbourhood project, not a registered charity: there are no tax receipts, just gratitude and more birdhouses.
SupportPage.etransferBody: The way most neighbours chip in: no fees, straight from your banking app.
SupportPage.cardBody: Apple Pay, Google Pay, or any card, through a hosted checkout that takes seconds.
SupportPage.pingBody: Pick an amount and leave your details, and we'll email you a transfer request for exactly that amount. Accept it in your banking app and that's it. Nothing is charged automatically, and your details are only ever used to send that one request.

PrivacyPage.title: Privacy
PrivacyPage.intro: Perch Trail is a small art project. We try to collect as little information from you as possible, and we don't share, sell, or reuse it for anything else.
PrivacyPage.whatWeAskHeading: What we ask for when you request a profile
PrivacyPage.nameItem: Your name: how you'd like to be credited. This goes on your birdhouse's public profile.
PrivacyPage.emailItem: Your email: so we can send you your profile link and your access code. This is not shown publicly.
PrivacyPage.communityQuestionItem: A community question answer: a quick anti-bot check, only ever seen by us.
PrivacyPage.afterSetup: Once your profile is set up, you can add more if you want: a few words about the artist, a few words about the birdhouse, a photo, a pin on the map. All of that is optional, edited by you with your access code, and only shown publicly if you decide to share it.
PrivacyPage.emailDeletionHeading: Your email: when we delete it
PrivacyPage.emailReason: We keep your email for one reason: so we can help you recover your access code if you lose it. If that happens, send us the URL of your profile from the original welcome email and we'll email you a new code.
PrivacyPage.emailDeletionDetail: We delete a requester's email twelve months after their profile goes live. After that the profile continues to exist, but the email is no longer on our servers. If you lose your access code after that, reach out and we'll work with you to get you a new one through whatever information you still have.
PrivacyPage.dontShareMarketing: We don't share it with third parties for marketing.
PrivacyPage.dontUseOtherwise: We don't use it for anything other than what's described above.
PrivacyPage.dontShowHostName: We don't show the caretaker / host name publicly. The map shows the birdhouse, not the person.
PrivacyPage.serviceProvidersText: We use Vercel to host the site, Supabase to store data, Cloudflare Turnstile for bot checking, and Resend to send the welcome email. Each of them processes the minimum they need to do their job.
PrivacyPage.questionsText: If you want your data removed sooner, or if anything about this note feels unclear, reach out through the contact form on <getInvolvedLink>Get Involved</getInvolvedLink>.

TermsPage.title: Terms
TermsPage.intro: Perch Trail is a small community art project. These terms are short on purpose. If something is unclear, just ask.
TermsPage.requestingText: Anyone who has made or hosts a birdhouse in the neighbourhood is welcome to ask for a profile on the map. We review requests by hand and may decline any request without a specific reason, usually because it looks like spam, bot traffic, or is clearly off-topic.
TermsPage.whatGoesPublicText: When we approve your request, the name you provide, your photo, your map location, and your short note are published on your profile. Your email is not shown and is kept only as described in our <privacyLink>privacy note</privacyLink>.
TermsPage.editingText: You can edit your profile at any time using the access code we email you. By default, edits are reviewed before going live. Live profiles stay visible while an edit is being reviewed.
TermsPage.removingText: If you want your profile taken down, reach out through the contact form on <getInvolvedLink>Get Involved</getInvolvedLink> and we'll take care of it.
TermsPage.changesText1: Perch Trail evolves. We may archive old profiles, change how the map works, or adjust the project's direction over time. We'll try to be transparent about any changes that affect you.
TermsPage.changesText2: Tweaks happen, but the spirit of the project, and the care we take with people's information, will not.
TermsPage.noWarrantyText: The site is provided as-is. We're doing our best, but we can't guarantee uninterrupted service or that everything will always work perfectly.

RecoverPage.intro1: No problem. Enter the URL of your profile (from the original welcome email) and the email you used to request it, and we'll email you a new code.
RecoverPage.intro2: Your previous code will stop working as soon as we send the new one.
RecoverPage.footerNote: We delete requester emails twelve months after a profile goes live. After that, recovery is no longer possible, so keep your welcome email somewhere safe.
